title: Fix rejected drain PR #183 (agent/drain/OS-curriculum-v2-conformance-133)
description:
Drain PR #183 (branch `agent/drain/OS-curriculum-v2-conformance-133`) was NOT merged by pr-auto-review (llm-rejected).
Repair it ON THE EXISTING BRANCH — do NOT create a new branch or a second PR:
1. `git fetch origin agent/drain/OS-curriculum-v2-conformance-133 && git checkout agent/drain/OS-curriculum-v2-conformance-133`
2. Address EVERY reason below.
3. Run `npm test` until green.
4. Commit and `git push origin agent/drain/OS-curriculum-v2-conformance-133` — the reviewer re-reviews at the new SHA.

## Rejection reasons (verbatim)
- [major] CLI argument parsing bug: In agents/speak.mjs line 118-135, the CLI parsing logic incorrectly handles the --output flag by skipping the first positional argument (agent name) but then doesn't properly extract the agent name from args[0] — the code increments i++ on line 121 but then never uses the extracted agent value. This would cause the agent variable to be undefined. — Reframe: Fix the CLI parsing logic to properly extract agent name from args[0] before processing flags, or use a proper argument parser library.
- [major] Missing executable permission on stub piper: In tests/speak.test.mjs line 92, the stub piper script is created without executable permissions, which would cause execSync() to fail when trying to run it. — Reframe: Add chmodSync(piperPath, 0o755) after writing the stub script to make it executable.
- [minor] Inconsistent error handling: In agents/speak.mjs line 49 and 62, debug messages use console.debug which may not be visible in all environments, while CLI errors use console.error. — Reframe: Use consistent logging approach (either structured logging or remove debug messages entirely for production code).
- [minor] Hardcoded path separator: In agents/speak.mjs line 85, the agent name sanitization uses regex /[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g which assumes Unix-style filenames but doesn't account for Windows path separators. — Reframe: Use a more robust sanitization that also removes path separators or use path.basename() for safety.
